insights.claim_template: Financing costs the book more than its financial assets return: financial expense of {money:financial_expense} against financial income of {money:financial_income} leaves a net cost of {money:net_financial}, {measure:graded_share} of {money:graded_base}.
insights.formula: Financial income − financial expense, against operating EBITDA

measures.label: Net financial result as a share of ebitda

narrative.explanation: Financing costs the book more than its financial assets return: financial expense of RON 171,045.53 against financial income of RON 6,902.16 leaves a net cost of RON -164,143.37, 15.5% of RON 1,058,532.69. Graded medium: the amount at stake is 15.5% of ebitda, against the ladder printed beside this finding. The financial result is graded against the operating earnings it sits beside, because the question is how much of the bottom line the company earned by trading rather than by lending or borrowing.
narrative.reason: the advisory lane was not invoked for this build
narrative.so_what: Separate the operating result from the financial one when judging the trading business. Financial income earned on assets or affiliates does not repeat because trading improved.

insights.claim_template: {measure:depreciated_share} of gross PP&E is already depreciated; the remaining net book value of {money:net_book_value} carries {measure:remaining_book_life} of life at the current annual charge of {money:annual_da}.
insights.formula: Accumulated depreciation ÷ gross PP&E; net book value ÷ annual D&A = remaining book life

measures.label: Remaining book life at current charge

narrative.explanation: 40.5% of gross PP&E is already depreciated; the remaining net book value of RON 3,241,585.45 carries 8.1 years of life at the current annual charge of RON 400,705.85. Graded low: the amount at stake is 40.5% of gross pp&e, against the ladder printed beside this finding. Depreciation is graded against the asset base that produced it, so a factory and a courier are compared on the share of their OWN gross PP&E already written off rather than on an absolute charge.
narrative.reason: the advisory lane was not invoked for this build
narrative.so_what: Ask for the fixed-asset register by acquisition year and the committed capex plan. A book this far through its depreciation life either has replacement spending ahead of it or is running assets past their useful life, and the two have very different cash consequences.

insights.rank_basis: Ranked by severity level, then by materiality descending; ties broken by detector id ascending. The top 5 carry into the executive summary.

severity.why: Depreciation is graded against the asset base that produced it, so a factory and a courier are compared on the share of their OWN gross PP&E already written off rather than on an absolute charge.

insights.title: Asset base is late in its depreciation life

insights.claim: RON 51,498.35 of operating income is other operating income and provision reversals rather than trading margin — 4.9% of RON 1,058,532.69; the operating cash proxy is RON 851,398.17 against an EBITDA of RON 1,058,532.69, a conversion of 80.4%.
insights.claim_template: {money:non_trading} of operating income is other operating income and provision reversals rather than trading margin — {measure:graded_share} of {money:graded_base}; the operating cash proxy is {money:cash_proxy} against an EBITDA of {money:ebitda}, a conversion of {measure:cash_conversion}.
insights.formula: (Other operating income + provision reversals) ÷ EBITDA; operating cash proxy ÷ EBITDA; capitalised own work

measures.label: Other operating income and provision reversals
Non-trading income as a share of ebitda

narrative.explanation: RON 51,498.35 of operating income is other operating income and provision reversals rather than trading margin — 4.9% of RON 1,058,532.69; the operating cash proxy is RON 851,398.17 against an EBITDA of RON 1,058,532.69, a conversion of 80.4%. Graded low: the amount at stake is 4.9% of ebitda, against the ladder printed beside this finding. Non-trading income is graded against the EBITDA it is inside, so the severity answers "how much of this margin is not trading" rather than "is this a big number".
narrative.reason: the advisory lane was not invoked for this build
narrative.so_what: Strip the non-trading income out before applying any multiple. Provision reversals and other operating income do not recur, and an EBITDA that leans on them overstates the run rate.

insights.rank_basis: Ranked by severity level, then by materiality descending; ties broken by detector id ascending. The top 5 carry into the executive summary.

severity.why: Non-trading income is graded against the EBITDA it is inside, so the severity answers "how much of this margin is not trading" rather than "is this a big number".

insights.title: Part of EBITDA is not trading income

insights.claim: The net trade float is RON 390,848.73: RON 1,382,531.56 owed by customers against RON 991,682.83 owed to suppliers — 54 days of sales outstanding against 42 days of payables (RON 1,019,182.83 of balance-sheet payables over RON 8,935,369.45 of total operating expense, on 365 days), a gap of 12 days.
insights.claim_template: The net trade float is {money:float}: {money:trade_receivables} owed by customers against {money:trade_payables} owed to suppliers — {measure:dso} of sales outstanding against {measure:dpo} of payables ({money:dpo_payables} of balance-sheet payables over {money:total_operating_expense} of total operating expense, on {measure:period_days}), a gap of {measure:float_days}.
insights.formula: DSO = trade receivables net ÷ revenue × the period's days; DPO = balance-sheet payables ÷ total operating expense × the period's days (the ratio table's one DPO, engine.ratios.table.dpo_days); float = trade receivables net − trade payables

measures.label: Days payables outstanding (on total operating cost)

narrative.explanation: The net trade float is RON 390,848.73: RON 1,382,531.56 owed by customers against RON 991,682.83 owed to suppliers — 54 days of sales outstanding against 42 days of payables (RON 1,019,182.83 of balance-sheet payables over RON 8,935,369.45 of total operating expense, on 365 days), a gap of 12 days. Graded low: the amount at stake is 4.2% of revenue, against the ladder printed beside this finding. Trade float is a claim on a year of trading, so it is graded as a share of that year's revenue — the same base both day counts already annualise against.
narrative.reason: the advisory lane was not invoked for this build
narrative.so_what: Compare the collection gap with the credit terms actually granted. Where suppliers fund the cycle, that funding is a payables line that can be withdrawn, not a permanent source.

insights.rank_basis: Ranked by severity level, then by materiality descending; ties broken by detector id ascending. The top 5 carry into the executive summary.

severity.why: Trade float is a claim on a year of trading, so it is graded as a share of that year's revenue — the same base both day counts already annualise against.

insights.claim: The current ratio of 1.95× falls to 1.94× once RON 21,000.00 of non-trade receivables is removed; the cash ratio is 0.13×.
insights.claim_template: The current ratio of {measure:current_ratio} falls to {measure:current_ratio_trade_only} once {money:non_trade} of non-trade receivables is removed; the cash ratio is {measure:cash_ratio}.
insights.formula: Current ratio recomputed with non-trade receivables (intercompany, other debtors, supplier advances, tax recoverable) removed from current assets

narrative.explanation: The current ratio of 1.95× falls to 1.94× once RON 21,000.00 of non-trade receivables is removed; the cash ratio is 0.13×.
